subject: Physics
prompt: Volume of a body “X” of aluminium is twice volume of another body “Y” made of aluminium. What can you say about the masses of the two bodies?
options: Mass of “Y” is greater than mass of “X”.
Mass of “X” is greater than mass of “Y”.
Mass of “X” and mass of “Y” are equal.
Mass of “X” and “Y” are not comparable.
explanation_steps: Both bodies are made of aluminium, so they have the same density.
Mass = density × volume, therefore mass of X is twice the mass of Y.
Mass of X is greater than mass of Y.

subject: Physics
prompt: A vector has X-component of 50 units. Find the Y-component and the resultant vector respectively, if the resultant vector makes an angle of 30° with the y-axis (cos 30° = 0.866, sin 30° = 0.5).
explanation_steps: The resultant makes 30° with the y-axis, so its x-component is R × sin(30°) and y-component is R × cos(30°).
Given X-component = 50 = R × 0.5 ⇒ R = 100 units.
Y-component = 100 × 0.866 = 86.6 units.
Therefore Y-component and resultant are 86.6 units and 100 units.

subject: Physics
prompt: A man walks 40 m due east, then 50 m due north, then 60 m due west. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant respectively (tan⁻¹(0.4) = 21.8°).
explanation_steps: Net displacement east-west: 40 m east − 60 m west = −20 m (20 m west).
Net north-south: 50 m north.
Angle from north: tan⁻¹(20/50) = tan⁻¹(0.4) ≈ 21.8° west of north, i.e. 21.8° north west.

subject: Physics
prompt: The ideal mechanical advantage (I.M.A.) of a simple machine is always
options: greater than the actual mechanical advantage.
less than the actual mechanical advantage.
equal to the actual mechanical advantage.
dependent upon the nature of the simple machine.
explanation_steps: Ideal mechanical advantage assumes no friction or energy losses.
Actual mechanical advantage is reduced by friction, so I.M.A. is always greater than or equal to A.M.A.
In real machines I.M.A. > A.M.A.
